meta.title: 1962 Canadian BCP, psalter appointment and weekday cycle
meta.description: The ordinary weekday psalm table, the selections of psalms, and the rubrics governing how the Psalter is appointed to be read, from the official ACC 1962 BCP.

sources.ref: The Book of Common Prayer (1962), General Synod of the Anglican Church of Canada, The Order how the Psalter is Appointed to be Read, Selections of Psalms, and A Table of Psalms for Ordinary Weekdays, printed pages xlix to lv
sources.note: Local copy /tmp/opencode/bcp1962-acc.pdf, text extracted with pdftotext -layout.

caveats: Psalm appointments are raw strings because of parts, alternatives, and verse ranges.
The two month sets are the witness's alternating-column table.
The Eucharist rubrics are stored for fidelity but are not used by a Daily Office experience.

rubrics.monthlyCycle: The Psalter is to be read through once a month as it is there appointed, unless the Psalms are read according to one of the Tables following.
rubrics.day31: On the thirty-first day of the month, the Psalms for the thirtieth are to be used, or else one of the selections found in the Table of Selections following.
rubrics.weekdayOmission: Upon any weekday for which no Proper Psalms are appointed, one Psalm may be omitted, provided that one Psalm, or one numbered portion of a Psalm, is always retained.
rubrics.twoMonthTable: A Table is provided according to which the Psalter may be read through in a period of two months. It is intended for use on those days on which the shortened service is permitted.
rubrics.ordinary: Psalms for special occasions not already provided are appointed by the Ordinary.
rubrics.gloriaPatri: The Gloria Patri is to be said or sung after each Psalm, or numbered portion of a Psalm, or after the whole selection of Psalms. It may be omitted on the last three days of Holy Week.
rubrics.chantMark: In the Psalter the sign / indicates the place in each verse where the chant changes. In reading, a pause is made at this sign.
rubrics.hellNote: Note that the word hell where used in the Psalter means the place of the dead.
rubrics.selectionsUse: The following Selections may be used on the thirty-first day of the month. They may also be used with the Litany, or at the Service for Young People, or at Compline.
rubrics.psalm95Note: Psalm 95 is to be said or sung in full.
